descriptors.definition: Promoters must contribute a minimum percentage towards public or composite issues as specified by regulations. Issuers lacking an identifiable promoter are exempt from this requirement.
inclusion: Issuers with identifiable promoters
Public issues
Composite issues
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general public share allotments by imposing mandatory skin-in-the-game requirements on promoters.

descriptors.definition: The requirement for minimum promoters' contribution does not apply if an issuer lacks an identifiable promoter. It also excludes certain frequently traded issuers meeting specific listing and investor grievance redressal criteria.
inclusion: Issuers with no identifiable promoter
Issuers with shares frequently traded for at least three years with high investor complaint redressal
exclusion: Issuers with identifiable promoters failing the trading history or compliance criteria
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard minimum contribution mandates by waiving lock-in and equity commitment thresholds under specific compliance conditions.

descriptors.concept_name: Exemptions and Pricing for Minimum Promoters' Contribution
descriptors.definition: Minimum promoters' contribution requirements are waived for issuers without identifiable promoters or those meeting specific three-year trading and listing compliance thresholds. Excess promoter subscriptions must be priced at higher of regulation-specified formulas or the actual issue price.
inclusion: Issuers lacking an identifiable promoter
Issuers maintaining three-year trading and 95 percent investor complaint redressal
exclusion: Issuers failing board composition norms without regularized disclosure cure
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard contribution rules by providing conditional exemptions and pricing floors for excess commitments.

descriptors.concept_name: Minimum Promoters' Contribution Mandates and Escrow
descriptors.definition: Promoters must contribute twenty percent of the proposed issue size or post-issue capital prior to the issue opening date. Funds must be deposited in an escrow account with a scheduled commercial bank until issue proceeds are released.
inclusion: Public issue equity and convertible securities
Composite issue contributions excluding rights components
exclusion: Uncalled or late-deposited promoter funds falling past the one-day pre-opening window
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from excess promoter contributions by enforcing strict pre-issue deposit timelines and escrow holding mechanisms.

descriptors.definition: Certain specified securities acquired via non-cash consideration involving asset revaluation or capitalization of intangibles cannot count toward minimum promoters' contribution. Bonus issues originating from revaluation reserves or unrealized profits are similarly excluded.
inclusion: Securities acquired for non-cash consideration with revaluation components
Bonus issues from unrealized profits
exclusion: Securities acquired via tribunal or court-approved amalgamation schemes under the Companies Act
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from eligible contribution shares by barring artificial capital inflations and unverified asset write-ups.

descriptors.definition: Specified securities held by promoters are subjected to mandatory non-transferability lock-in periods following further public offers or initial public allotments. The exact duration depends on whether issue proceeds are utilized for capital expenditure.
inclusion: Minimum promoters' contribution including AIF or FVCI holdings
Promoter holdings exceeding minimum contribution thresholds
exclusion: Securities lent for green shoe options during the lending period
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from excess holding lock-ins by applying extended durations when issue proceeds fund capital expenditures.

descriptors.concept_name: Promoter Lock-in and Capital Expenditure Rules
descriptors.definition: Promoter-held specified securities must remain non-transferable for statutory lock-in timeframes determined by the deployment of issue proceeds. Special rights equity shares remain locked-in until converting into ordinary voting shares.
inclusion: Eighteen-month and three-year lock-in durations for minimum contributions
SR equity shares prior to conversion
exclusion: Ordinary transfers prior to lock-in expiry without regulatory exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity lock-ins through specialized conversion requirements imposed on superior voting rights shares.

descriptors.concept_name: Lock-in Exemptions and Pledging Rules for Promoters
descriptors.definition: Lock-in restrictions do not apply to securities temporarily lent to stabilising agents under green shoe options during the active loan window. Locked-in promoter shares can be pledged as loan collateral provided the borrowing satisfies specific corporate object financing criteria.
inclusion: Securities lent for green shoe price stabilization
Pledges for loans financing issue objects
exclusion: Pledges where loan sanctions exclude specified security backing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from absolute transfer bans by allowing conditional pledging to institutional lenders for valid business objects.

descriptors.concept_name: Lock-in Mechanics for Partly Paid Securities
descriptors.definition: Partly paid-up specified securities subject to lock-in must remain restricted until eighteen months after they become fully pari passu with public-issued securities. This rule applies when calls on promoter shares trail behind public issues.
inclusion: Partly paid promoter securities with delayed call-up values relative to public issues
exclusion: Fully paid-up securities governed by standard allotment-date schedules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from fully paid security lock-ins by pegging the expiry countdown to the date of equal footing establishment.

descriptors.concept_name: Marking and Depository Recording of Non-Transferability
descriptors.definition: Physical share certificates subject to lock-in must bear a non-transferable inscription along with the applicable time window. For dematerialized holdings, issuers must ensure depositories formally record the lock-in status.
inclusion: Physical certificates requiring text stamping
Dematerialized accounts requiring depository lock-in flags
exclusion: Free-floating securities unencumbered by lock-in obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from substantive lock-in criteria by focusing strictly on administrative marking and registry compliance enforcement.

descriptors.concept_name: Collateral Pledging of Locked-in Promoter Securities
descriptors.definition: Promoters may pledge locked-in securities as loan collateral with authorized institutional lenders if the borrowings directly fund approved issue objectives. Superior voting rights shares are expressly ineligible for such pledging arrangements.
inclusion: Pledges for loans to issuers or subsidiaries financing issue objects
Pledges sanctioned for excess promoter holdings
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general share pledging by tying permission directly to sanctioned loan terms and specific issue object financing.

descriptors.concept_name: Transferability and Due Diligence Standards for Offer Documents
descriptors.definition: Locked-in promoter securities may be transferred internally to other promoters, promoter groups, or controllers, provided the lock-in continues with the transferee. Lead managers must exercise due diligence to ensure financial statements are under six months old.
inclusion: Transfers between existing promoters, promoter groups, or persons in control
Verification of financial statement currency by lead managers
exclusion: Transfers of locked-in shares to external parties outside the promoter group
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from absolute transfer prohibitions by permitting intra-group promoter transfers while preserving remaining lock-in periods.
